newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds still struggling to crack 110-09.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds still struggling to crack 110-09.

text.p: September T-bond futures may get the impetus on Friday to pierce resistance at 110-09, a level they have been wrestling with more than three weeks, analysts said on Friday.
But the U.S. payroll report at 1230 GMT could send the contract either way, they said.

"Purely from a technical standpoint, T-bonds are fairly positive," said Andy Cossor, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London. "Although there is not a hugely strong uptrend in place, the last week or so has been constructive."
T-bonds were quoted at 110-01 at 1001 GMT, up 1/32 in automated trade.
Cossor said the contract must break above 110-09 -- a top that has been in place since the May 13 high -- to open the way for a test of former support from February at 111-16.
Support this session would come in at 109-28/29 congestion, then at 109-08/10, Cossor said.

"In event of a very strong payrolls, high earnings, it could retreat to lows of late May at 108-05 and below that former good daily resistance and support from March and April at 107-25," he said. "It will be in a bear phase if it gets through there."
Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast payrolls to rise by 219,000 in May after a 142,000 increase in April.
The unemployment rate was expected at 5.0 percent versus 4.9 percent while average hourly earnings were forecast to have risen 0.4 percent in the month.
September Eurodollars were quoted at 94.015, unchanged in automated trade.

Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, said the contract opened and closed at the same level on Thursday, forming a doji star on Japanese candlestick charts. This represented total confusion in the market.
"Prices are rising in a rising wedge with resistance at 94.045 for today," they said in a research note. "Rising wedges are ultimately bearish patterns."
They said they would sell any payroll induced bounce that does not move past 94.14. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
